channel.title: AI Waterside Podcast
channel.description: A daily brief on AI models, tooling and the creator side of the industry — what shipped, why it matters, and what to do about it.
channel.itunes:author: Austin Peechatt
channel.itunes:summary: A daily brief on AI models, tooling and the creator side of the industry — what shipped, why it matters, and what to do about it.

item.title: Tuesday, October 6
item.description: • Reflection Beam — an open‑source 501‑billion‑parameter text model for coding, agentic tasks and scientific work, offering near‑state‑of‑the‑art performance on commodity hardware. • Whirl — a self‑hostable full‑stack AI chat application built on Next.js and Convex that lets you plug any LLM, persistent memory and tools, enabling rapid internal chatbot prototypes. • AI System Design — a curated open‑source tutorial collection that walks developers through building LLM pipelines, retrieval‑augmented generation and autonomous agents, accelerating product prototyping. • Instinct — an AI agent you can add to chats on iOS, Android or web, coordinating plans and tasks without requiring participants to install app. • TikTok AI shopping assistant — a conversational tool that guides users through product details, sizing and checkout, keeping commerce inside the TikTok feed and streamlining purchases. • Cowork cloud version — moves model inference and the VM to remote servers, giving uninterrupted performance across devices and enhancing security by isolating sessions.

item.title: Monday, October 5
item.description: • Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 Flash Next — a 125‑billion‑parameter model that runs locally on consumer GPUs, enabling private coding, research, and image analysis. • Whirl — an open‑source self‑hosted AI chat platform built on Next.js and Convex that bundles top‑tier models, persistent memory, and optional tools. • AI System Design — an open‑source playbook that guides developers through LLM product architecture, retrieval‑augmented generation, and autonomous agent design. • Claude Code — Anthropic’s VS Code extension adds an inline sidebar for generating, refactoring, and explaining code with Claude, keeping the editor responsive. • OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Model Guide — a practical handbook that helps startups select model tiers, tune reasoning effort, and implement tool use for production. • X Video Composer — an AI‑powered caption editor using Grok that lets creators tweak, translate, and polish subtitles directly within the platform.

item.title: Sunday, October 4
item.description: • Strata — an open‑source package that lets you run the 125‑billion‑parameter Qwen 3.8 Flash Next model locally, providing a private, high‑performance AI assistant without cloud fees. • Claude Code — Anthropic’s VS Code extension that integrates Claude directly into the editor, now more stable and faster, ensuring reliable code suggestions and secure policy enforcement. • Whirl — a full‑stack, MIT‑licensed AI chat app built with Next.js and Convex that offers private, extensible conversations with persistent “living documents” and optional services. • AI System Design — a community‑maintained guide that walks developers through prompt engineering, retrieval‑augmented generation, autonomous agents, and a production checklist for safety and cost. • GPT‑6 Model Guide — a concise playbook for startups that maps latency, token budget, and reasoning needs to the appropriate OpenAI model, helping control costs. • Simon Willison’s hard‑budget‑cap recommendation — argues that every pay‑by‑usage service, especially AWS, should enforce a dollar limit that stops workloads, preventing surprise overspend.
item.content:encoded:

  • Whirl — a full‑stack, MIT‑licensed AI chat app built with Next.js and Convex that offers private, extensible conversations with persistent “living documents” and optional services.
  • AI System Design — a community‑maintained guide that walks developers through prompt engineering, retrieval‑augmented generation, autonomous agents, and a production checklist for safety and cost.
  • GPT‑6 Model Guide — a concise playbook for startups that maps latency, token budget, and reasoning needs to the appropriate OpenAI model, helping control costs.
  • Simon Willison’s hard‑budget‑cap recommendation — argues that every pay‑by‑usage service, especially AWS, should enforce a dollar limit that stops workloads, preventing surprise overspend.

item.title: Saturday, October 3
item.description: • Gemini 4 Argon — Google DeepMind's new large model with a million‑token window, enabling whole‑codebase reasoning and complex multi‑step tasks. • Claude Code — Anthropic's coding assistant update adds UI shortcuts, in‑session GitHub API calls, and prompt recovery to streamline debugging. • AI System Design — a community‑curated repository that provides runnable notebooks and Docker configs for building production‑grade LLM, RAG, and agent pipelines. • Strands Decider — a lightweight decision‑model library that strips the generation head from a decoder LLM, delivering millisecond‑scale scored choices for real‑time pipelines. • Meta’s Muse Gadgets — open‑source firmware and Linux SDK let developers attach Meta’s personal AI assistant to cheap hardware, creating custom voice‑controlled peripherals. • GPT‑6 model guide — a concise playbook that consolidates community best practices for selecting variants, tuning reasoning depth, and safely orchestrating tool calls.
item.content:encoded:
• Gemini 4 Argon — Google DeepMind's new large model with a million‑token window, enabling whole‑codebase reasoning and complex multi‑step tasks.
  • Claude Code — Anthropic's coding assistant update adds UI shortcuts, in‑session GitHub API calls, and prompt recovery to streamline debugging.
  • AI System Design — a community‑curated repository that provides runnable notebooks and Docker configs for building production‑grade LLM, RAG, and agent pipelines.
  • Strands Decider — a lightweight decision‑model library that strips the generation head from a decoder LLM, delivering millisecond‑scale scored choices for real‑time pipelines.
  • Meta’s Muse Gadgets — open‑source firmware and Linux SDK let developers attach Meta’s personal AI assistant to cheap hardware, creating custom voice‑controlled peripherals.
  • GPT‑6 model guide — a concise playbook that consolidates community best practices for selecting variants, tuning reasoning depth, and safely orchestrating tool calls.

item.title: Friday, October 2
item.description: • Meta’s Muse Gadgets — an open‑source kit that lets developers attach hardware to Meta’s personal AI agent, enabling tangible actions such as scheduling meetings or controlling lights. • Gemini 4 Argon — Google DeepMind’s frontier model with million‑token context, allowing extremely long, multi‑step reasoning for tasks like code reviews or legal research. • GPT‑6 model guide — a concise playbook that helps startups select the appropriate GPT‑6 variant, tune reasoning depth, and integrate tools into production pipelines. • Claude Code — an update that adds a fullscreen text‑selection helper, built‑in GitHub API, and prompt recovery shortcut, reducing friction for developers using Claude for coding assistance. • AI System Design — an open‑source collection of lessons and runnable code that guides building LLM‑powered retrieval, generation, and autonomous‑agent pipelines, accelerating prototype to production. • Strands Decider — a system‑one decision model from Strands that replaces the language head with fast option scoring, delivering sub‑second choices for agentic workflows.
